readings.title: Esau Marries Mahalath
readings.text: [Genesis 28:6] And Ěsaw saw that Yitsḥaq had blessed Yaʽaqoḇ and sent him away to Paddan Aram to take himself a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a command, saying, “Do not take a wife from the daughters of Kenaʽan,” [7] and that Yaʽaqoḇ obeyed his father and his mother and had gone to Paddan Aram. [8] So Ěsaw saw that the daughters of Kenaʽan did not please his father Yitsḥaq. [9] And Ěsaw went to Yishmaʽĕl and took Maḥalath the daughter of Yishmaʽĕl, Abraham’s son, the sister of Neḇayoth, to be his wife, besides the wives he had.

readings.title: Jacob's Dream at Bethel
readings.text: [Genesis 28:10] And Yaʽaqoḇ went out from Be’ĕrsheḇa and went toward Ḥaran. [11] And he came upon a place and stopped over for the night, for the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of that place and put it at his head, and he lay down in that place to sleep. [12] And he dreamed and saw a ladder set up on the earth, and its top reached to the heavens, and saw messengers of <dn>Elohim</dn> going up and coming down on it. [13] And see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood above it and said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Abraham your father and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yitsḥaq. The land on which you are lying, <dn>I</dn> give it to you and your seed.</dq> [14] <dq>“And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall break forth to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south. And in you and in your seed all the clans of the earth shall be blessed.</dq> [15] <dq>“And see, <dn>I</dn> am with you and shall guard you wherever you go, and shall bring you back to this land. For <dn>I</dn> am not going to leave you until <dn>I</dn> have done what <dn>I</dn> have spoken to you.”</dq> [16] And Yaʽaqoḇ awoke from his sleep and said, “Truly, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is in this place, and I did not know it.” [17] And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and this is the gate of the heavens!” [18] And Yaʽaqoḇ rose early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put at his head, set it up as a standing column, and poured oil on top of it. [19] And he called the name of that place Bĕyth Ěl, however, the name of the city was Luz previously. [20] And Yaʽaqoḇ made a vow, saying, “If <dn>Elohim</dn> is with me, and shall guard me in this way that I am going, and shall give me bread to eat and clothes to put on, [21] when I return in peace to my father’s house, then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be my <dn>Elohim</dn>. [22] “And this stone which I have set as a standing column shall be the house of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and of all that <dn>You</dn> give me, I shall certainly give a tenth to <dn>You</dn>.”

readings.title: Jacob Arrives in Haran
readings.text: [Genesis 29:1] And Yaʽaqoḇ lifted up his feet and went to the land of the people of the East. [2] And he looked and saw a well in the field, and see, three flocks of sheep lying by it, for out of that well they watered the flocks. And a large stone was on the well’s mouth. [3] And all the flocks would be gathered there, and they would roll the stone from the well’s mouth and water the sheep, and put the stone back in its place on the well’s mouth. [4] And Yaʽaqoḇ said to them, “My brothers, where are you from?” And they said, “We are from Ḥaran.” [5] And he said to them, “Do you know Laḇan the son of Naḥor?” And they said, “We know him.” [6] And he said to them, “Is he well?” And they said, “He is well. And see, Raḥĕl his daughter is coming with the sheep.” [7] And he said, “Look, it is still high day, it is not time for the livestock to be gathered together. Water the sheep, and go and feed them.” [8] But they said, “We are not able, until all the flocks are gathered together, and they have rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, then we shall water the sheep.” [9] While he was still speaking with them, Raḥĕl came with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess. [10] And it came to be, when Yaʽaqoḇ saw Raḥĕl the daughter of Laḇan his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laḇan his mother’s brother, that Yaʽaqoḇ went near and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laḇan his mother’s brother. [11] And Yaʽaqoḇ kissed Raḥĕl, and lifted up his voice and wept. [12] And Yaʽaqoḇ told Raḥĕl that he was her father’s relative and that he was Riḇqah’s son. And she ran and told her father. [13] And it came to be, when Laḇan heard the report about Yaʽaqoḇ his sister’s son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him and kissed him, and brought him to his house. So he told Laḇan all these words. [14] And Laḇan said to him, “Surely you are my bone and my flesh.”

readings.title: The Deceiver Deceived
readings.text: [Genesis 29:14] And he stayed with him a month of days. [15] And Laḇan said to Yaʽaqoḇ, “Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for naught? Tell me, what should your wages be?” [16] Now Laḇan had two daughters: the name of the elder was Lĕ’ah, and the name of the younger was Raḥĕl. [17] And the eyes of Lĕ’ah were weak, but Raḥĕl was lovely in form and lovely in appearance. [18] And Yaʽaqoḇ loved Raḥĕl, so he said, “I serve you seven years for Raḥĕl your younger daughter.” [19] And Laḇan said, “It is better that I give her to you than that I should give her to another man. Stay with me.” [20] So Yaʽaqoḇ served seven years for Raḥĕl, and they seemed to him but a few days because of the love he had for her. [21] And Yaʽaqoḇ said to Laḇan, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I might go in to her.” [22] And Laḇan gathered all the men of the place and made a feast. [23] And it came to be in the evening, that he took Lĕ’ah his daughter and brought her to Yaʽaqoḇ, and he went in to her. [24] And Laḇan gave his female servant Zilpah to his daughter Lĕ’ah as a female servant. [25] And it came to be in the morning, that see, it was Lĕ’ah. So he said to Laḇan, “What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Raḥĕl that I served you? Why then have you deceived me?” [26] And Laḇan said, “It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the first-born. [27] “Complete the week of this one, then we give you this one too, for the service which you shall serve with me still another seven years.” [28] And Yaʽaqoḇ did so and completed her week. Then he gave him his daughter Raḥĕl as wife also. [29] And Laḇan gave his female servant Bilhah to his daughter Raḥĕl as a female servant. [30] And he also went in to Raḥĕl, and he also loved Raḥĕl more than Lĕ’ah. And he served with Laḇan still another seven years.

readings.title: The Birth of the Patriarchs
readings.text: [Genesis 29:31] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw that Lĕ’ah was hated, and <dn>He</dn> opened her womb, but Raḥĕl was barren. [32] And Lĕ’ah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Re’uḇĕn, for she said, “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has looked on my affliction, because now my husband is going to love me.” [33] And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has heard that I am hated, <dn>He</dn> has therefore given me this son also.” And she called his name Shimʽon. [34] And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Now this time my husband is joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore his name was called Lĕwi. [35] And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Now I praise <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” Therefore she called his name Yehuḏah. Then she ceased bearing. [Genesis 30:1] And when Raḥĕl saw that she bore Yaʽaqoḇ no children, Raḥĕl envied her sister, and said to Yaʽaqoḇ, “Give me children, or else I die!” [2] And Yaʽaqoḇ’s anger burned against Raḥĕl, and he said, “Am I in the place of <dn>Elohim</dn>, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?” [3] And she said, “See, my female servant Bilhah; go in to her, and let her bear upon my knees, that I also may have children by her.” [4] So she gave him Bilhah her female servant as wife, and Yaʽaqoḇ went in to her. [5] And Bilhah conceived and bore Yaʽaqoḇ a son. [6] And Raḥĕl said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has rightly ruled my case, and has also heard my voice and given me a son.” Therefore she called his name Dan. [7] And Raḥĕl’s female servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Yaʽaqoḇ a second son. [8] And Raḥĕl said, “With wrestlings of <dn>Elohim</dn> I have wrestled with my sister, and I have overcome.” So she called his name Naphtali. [9] And when Lĕ’ah saw that she had ceased bearing, she took Zilpah her female servant and gave her to Yaʽaqoḇ as wife. [10] And Lĕ’ah’s female servant Zilpah bore Yaʽaqoḇ a son. [11] And Lĕ’ah said, “A troop comes!” So she called his name Gaḏ. [12] And Lĕ’ah’s female servant Zilpah bore Yaʽaqoḇ a second son. [13] And Lĕ’ah said, “For my happiness! For daughters shall call me happy.” So she called his name Ashĕr. [14] And Re’uḇĕn went in the days of wheat harvest and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother Lĕ’ah. And Raḥĕl said to Lĕ’ah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.” [15] But she said to her, “Is it a small matter that you have taken away my husband? Would you take away my son’s mandrakes also?” And Raḥĕl said, “Therefore let him lie with you tonight for your son’s mandrakes.” [16] And when Yaʽaqoḇ came out of the field in the evening, Lĕ’ah went out to meet him and said, “You have to come in to me, for I have certainly hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” And he lay with her that night. [17] And <dn>Elohim</dn> listened to Lĕ’ah, and she conceived and bore Yaʽaqoḇ a fifth son. [18] And Lĕ’ah said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has given me my hire, because I have given my female servant to my husband.” So she called his name Yissasḵar. [19] And Lĕ’ah conceived again and bore Yaʽaqoḇ a sixth son. [20] And Lĕ’ah said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has endowed me with a good endowment. Now my husband is going to dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons.” So she called his name Zeḇulun. [21] And afterward she bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah. [22] And <dn>Elohim</dn> remembered Raḥĕl, and <dn>Elohim</dn> listened to her and opened her womb. [23] And she conceived and bore a son, and said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has taken away my reproach.” [24] And she called his name Yosĕph, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> add to me another son.”
